acceptance: Every Trunk push run on develop in the exact window (UTC start and end recorded) and every attempt is enumerated; every run with any red attempt is listed with run id, attempt outcomes, failing job and test, failure signature, first and latest outcomes, cause, platform sensitivity, recovery action and evidence confidence recorded separately. 'Unknown - evidence unavailable' is allowed with a named owner and the missing evidence. Persistent failures are also grouped into incidents. The table is recorded on this item.

Independent stale-base composition incidents are counted per week and compared with the governance threshold of about one a week; if exceeded, an owner review of reinstating the up-to-date requirement and its refresh cost is requested
Each recurring cause (two or more runs or incidents) has an item, existing or new, linked here; the linked items are the fixes that trunk-red-rate-target-20261024 waits for

The classification states how the red-trunk gate and arm gate (trunk-red-stops-further-merges, trunk-arm-gate-blames-newest-red-run-20261022) treated these runs, and whether that explains reds clearing without a revert

Evidence needed for the classification (logs, job records, attempt history) is saved on or linked from this item before it expires (artifacts have 7-, 14- or 30-day retention, so some evidence may already be gone)
context:

Source: independent review of the PR-checks versus Trunk split on 2026-10-24 (develop a56738db4; run history 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-24: 465 merged PRs; 466 Trunk push runs covering 465 unique head SHAs, because runs 38911870169 and 38911871641 share one SHA; Trunk coverage push runs only exist from 2026-10-21). Run logs are believed to expire after about 90 days (2027-01-08), but this was not checked against repository settings, and artifacts have explicit 7-, 14- and 30-day retention, so evidence can disappear much earlier; do the classification promptly.
description: The captured data lists 59 of 466 Trunk push runs on develop (12.66%; 59 of 465 completed runs, 12.69%, since one was in progress) whose latest attempt failed between 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-24, on 13 dates and 59 distinct head SHAs. That is neither a first-attempt rate nor an any-attempt rate: run lists show only the latest attempt and the capture has no attempt history or logs. The data contains two revert-titled Trunk runs; recovery and cause remain unclassified for every run, and two of the latest sampled runs (40071524792, 40071232825) are still red. So the data does not show that most reds were flakes or that the others cleared by revert. Enumerate every Trunk push run in the exact window and every attempt, including runs whose first or an intermediate attempt failed even if the latest passed. Classify cause, platform sensitivity and recovery as separate fields, because they overlap: cause (flaky or non-deterministic test, infrastructure or runner or API failure, stale-base composition between concurrent squash merges, real regression, unknown), platform sensitivity (for example Python 3.12 only: PR fast runs on 3.14 at ci.yml:867 and Trunk fast on 3.12 at trunk.yml:33), recovery action (rerun, revert, fix-forward, quarantine, none), and evidence confidence. Passing on rerun shows intermittency, not its root cause. Group persistent failures into incidents as well as listing runs. Count independent stale-base incidents, not every later red run carrying the same defect, against the governance threshold: docs/internal/merge-queue-governance.md:214-216 says that more than about one a week means the owner should consider reinstating the up-to-date requirement, so exceeding it triggers an owner review of reinstatement and its refresh cost (develop rulesets currently have strict_required_status_checks_policy false and no merge queue). This classification is the baseline that coverage selection needs before going live; the rate target lives in trunk-red-rate-target-20261024. Do not duplicate the existing red-stop, culprit-attribution and producer-check items; link them.
